newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition extends lead in Mexico elections - poll.
newsitem.headline: Opposition extends lead in Mexico elections - poll.

text.p: With little more than a week until key mid-term Mexican elections, the opposition looks poised to take control of the lower house of Congress, according to a Reforma newspaper poll printed on Friday.

The survey of 1,216 voters in 32 states projected that President Ernesto Zedillo's party would win just 36.7 percent of the national vote for congress, way below the level it needs for a majority in the lower house.

Some 30.1 percent would vote for the right-wing National Action Party (PAN) and 25.5 percent supported the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), Reforma said. These figures were reached after eliminating likely abstainers and undecided voters.
The poll is one of the last indicators of public sentiment in the elections, as Mexican law prohibits polls being published after Friday night.
While the PRI is expected to win the largest number of deputies, a coalition of the opposition parties could stop the PRI's practice of rubber-stamping bills sent by the president.
Of those polled, 47 percent believed the elections would be clean, compared to 42 percent that did not believe elections would be fair.
Reforma said the confidence level had improved from the 1994 presidential elections, when a majority of voters expected tinkering with votes.
The survey was conducted between June 20-24. No margin of error was given.
